significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—“transmission strength scales with the overlap between teacher and student empirical NTK / gradient subspaces”—plus the causal result that permutation alignment can restore transmission, thereby predicting transmission across graded model relationships rather than merely locating a trait representation. This addresses the specific shared-base-model dependence reported by Cloud et al. (2025), while Jacot et al. (2018) and Ainsworth et al. (2023) support the relevance of tangent geometry and permutation alignment; the conclusion would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic explanation, although “scales with” does not specify a precise functional form. Failure of both overlap scaling and re-basin restoration would informatively rule out tangent-space overlap and basis mismatch as sufficient explanations, and true versus false outcomes are distinguishable. Topic substitution would leave only a generic proposal to extend subliminal learning and would not merit this score; the quantitative overlap law and cross-initialization restoration prediction are the claim-specific reasons for scoring above the topic median.

reach.justification: The principal handle is “teacher-student tangent overlap,” operationalized as “subspace overlap (principal angles / kernel alignment),” which could serve as an ex-ante predictor of whether a model pair will transmit traits before distillation or fine-tuning; “aligning a student to a teacher via permutation symmetry” is additionally an intervention handle. Because the asserted relation predicts that greater re-extracted overlap yields stronger transmission, its substance can survive model-specific recalibration rather than merely providing a procedure that must rediscover the result from scratch. The hypothesis ranges over shared, diverged, and independently initialized models, with likely uptake by researchers and practitioners auditing model lineages or distillation pipelines, though it does not establish transfer across architectures or modalities. Topic substitution would remove both the overlap predictor and alignment intervention and therefore would not retain this reach score.
